(I)--(सहस्राक्ष, देवेन्द्र, etc.). A लोकपाल। He and three other लोकपालस् have their cities on the मान- sottara mountain in पुष्करद्वीप;

Deprived पृथु of his sacrificial horse during the hundredth अश्वमेध। Urged by Atri, पृथु's son pursued Indra, when the latter aban- doned the house and disappeared. A second time Indra deprived पृथु of his horse; when the king's men pursued him, he left the horse and went away in disguise. This enraged पृथु, who aimed his arrow at Indra but was pacified by ब्रह्मा in the name of धर्म। A reconcilia- tion was effected when पृथु embraced him.
5: Ib. IV. १६. २४; १९. १०-17, १९-22, २६-39; २०. १८.

7: Ib. V. 4. 3 and 8.
During हिरण्यकशिपु's absence at Mandara hill, Indra captured his queen and took her to his heavenly abode. नारद intervened and set her at liberty.

Took up his वज्र against Cyavana for allowing अश्विन्स् to partake of सोम juice. But Cyavana's तपस् tied down his arms, when Indra yielded.
9: Ib. IX. 3. २५, २६.
Assumed the form of a bull over which Kakustha rode and defeated Asuras in a battle. Made the crying मान्- धात suckle his finger.
१०: Ib. IX. 6. १२-15, ३१; Vi. IV. 2. २९-32.
Prevented Rohita from entering [page१-188+ ४६] his city for six years: Awarded हरिश्चन्द्र a golden chariot after his पुरुषमेध।
११: भा. VII. 7. १७-20, २३.
Robbed Sagara's sacrifi- cial horse and left it near Kapila's hermitage.
१२: Ib. IX. 8. 8 and १०.
Performed a sacrifice which was attended by वसिष्ठ.
१३: Ib. IX. १३. 1 and 2.
Joined the gods in तारकामय war.
१४: Ib. IX. १४. 7.
Asked Gandharvas to take back उर्वशी living with पुरूरवस्.
१५: Ib. IX. १४. २६.
Helped by राजि, gave back his kingdom. After his death, his sons refused to give back the kingdom, and Indra slew all of them.
१६: Ib. IX. १७. १३-16; Br. III. ६७. ८७-105.
Cursed by दुर्वास, he lost all fortune. The three worlds became empty. वरुण and other gods conferred with ब्रह्मा. Finding no means to restore their fortunes, they repaired to Hari Ajita when ब्रह्मा belauded Hari as महाविभूति। Hari advised them to secure Bali's alliance.
१७: भा. VIII. 5. १६-50; 6. ३०-31.
When the देवासुर war broke out, the gods fought with Bali who defeated them. At that time Indra prayed to Hari for help. Encouraged by the latter, the war was renewed and Bali was defeated. At this Jambha offered to fight Indra and disabled his elephant. मातलि supplied a chariot and Jambha's head was cut off. Namuci, Bala and पाक attacked Indra. The latter two were slain. Namuci proved too much for Indra's वज्र। A voice from the sky told Indra that Namuci could not be crushed by a wet or dry thing. Then Indra used फेन (foam) and vanquished him. Bali in the meantime gathered strength and beseiged Indra. Indra sought counsel of बृहस्पति who cared for his welfare, and as advised by the latter, he abandoned the city.
१८: Ib. VIII. १०. २४ and २८, ४१-53; ११. 1-४०; १५. २४-33; M. २२. ६०-61; २९. ११; ३१. १२.

१९: भा. VIII. २३. १९ and २४.
Defeated by Arjuna who got the सभा made by Maya. Arjuna for a short time shared his throne. Defeated by Arjuna at खाण्डव. His city visited by Arjuna in the course of a search for the dead children of the द्वारका Bra1hman2a.
२०: Ib. X. ८९. ३४[4], ४४.

२१: Ib. X. ८९. ३४[5].

२२: Ib. XI. 4. 7 and १६.
sent nymphs to disturb मार्कण्डेय's व्रत but in vain.
२३: Ib. XII. 8. १५-31.

२४: Ib. XII. 6. १७-23.

२५: Ib. X. ६८. २८ and ३४.

२६: Ib. X. ७४. १३.
For his sake Hari went to Bali in the disguise of a ब्राह्मण.
२७: Ib. X. ७२. २५.
Once he sat with इन्द्राणी in his सभा sur- rounded by all gods. In his pride he did not welcome his preceptor बृहस्पति in the proper way. The latter went away home at once and concealed himself from the gods. On this the Asuras attacked the gods. Indra repented and on ब्रह्मा's advice appointed विश्वरूप as his preceptor. Having been initiated into the विद्या वर्म नारायणात्म- कम्, he was enjoying his original prosperity. One day Indra discovered that a part of विश्वरूप's offerings went to the Asuras and therefore cut off his head in anger. Thus he incurred the sin of ब्रह्महत्या। After a year, in order to rid himself of it he divided his sin into four parts among (1) the earth with the boon that dug portion should get filled up, (2) the waters with the boon of increasing volume when mixed up, (3) trees with the boon that branches cut off grow again, and (4) women with the boon of ever cherishing the passion of love. The saline soil, bubbles and foam, gum and monthly discharges respectively represent the ब्रह्महत्या sin.
२८: Ib. VI. 7. 2-४०; 8. ४२; 9. 4-११.
With वज्र made of दधीचि's bones (made by त्वष्ट्र् from sun's तेजस्--मत्स्य प्।), Indra attacked वृत्र as Rudra attacked Yama. The encounter took place on the banks of the नर्मदा in the first त्रेतायुग। Battle described. Seeing his friends escaping in fright, वृत्र en- couraged them to stand and fight. He also disabled Indra's ऐरावत, and addressed him at length. Indra cut off one of his arms. With the remaining arm वृत्र hit Indra while the वज्र slipped from his hands causing concern to the gods. [page१-190+ ४३] Encouraged by the straight speech of वृत्र, Indra took up his वज्र and cut off his other arm. वृत्र swallowed him; but Indra, the vanquisher of Bala, got out of his stomach and cut off his head. Indra's regret at the murder of another ब्राह्मण. The sin of brahmicide, says the legend, took the disguise of a चण्डाल woman and ran towards him in a terrific form when he entered the lake मानस and lived in the lotus stalks for a thousand years. Invited by ब्राह्म- णस्, he performed an अश्वमेध and got rid of his sins.
२९: Ib. VIII. १०. १३-33; ११. १०-27; १२. 3-३३; १३. 4-२१.
Father of three sons Jayanta and others through Pau- लोमी. Getting to know that his mother Diti was observing a vow to get a child to slay him he offered to do service to her. Once he found her slack in her duty. He entered the womb and cut the child into seven pieces and each of these again into seven. At her request he offered to her to give them the rank of gods, by name मरुत्स्,
३०: Ib. VI. १८. 7, ३७, ५४, ५६-77; M. 7. ५०-65; ६९. ६०; १४६. २०, २८-44, ४५-55; Br. III. 5. ५५-79; IV. २०. ४४.
who were allowed to share in the यज्ञस्। Diti thought of another son वज्रान्ग who bound Indra and placed him before her. Was released on mediation from ब्रह्मा and कश्यप.
३०: a) M. १४६. ४५-55.
Reported to कृष्ण the wicked deeds of Naraka. Got a gift of मणिपर्वत of Naraka from कृष्ण.
३१: भा. X. ५९. 1 [1] and 2, २२[3]; Vi. V. २९. 1-१५.
Visited by कृष्ण and सत्यभामा. At the latter's wish, पारिजात was removed without any intimation. Indra, induced by इन्द्राणि attacked him with all gods. Kubera, वरुण and others were defeated. Indra himself offered resist- ance. गरुड disabled his elephant and Indra retreated. सत्यभामा made fun of him ‘Do not run, Lord of इन्द्राणी.’ Indra apologised. कृष्ण answered that Indra was not in the wrong as he (कृष्ण) took the offensive. Indra asked pardon and begged that his son बीभत्सु be protected. कृष्ण told him that पारिजात would go back to him when he left the mortal world. Returned to his city with all gods.
३२: Ib. V. ३७. १६; भा. X. ५९. ३८-39; [६५ (V) 5], [३७-51]; [६६. (V)] whole; [६७ (V) 1-३७]; Vi. V. ३०. ५१-70; ३१. 1-१०.
The God of rain: Sent torrents of showers on Gokula when कृष्ण protected his friends by holding up the hill [page१-191+ ५०] Govardhana. At this Indra and Surabhi came to visit him. Indra asked for pardon. Told by कृष्ण that he was humi- liated for his own good. In the company of Surabhi, Indra got कृष्ण bathed with the waters of the गङ्गा and called him Govinda. Returned to his region.

--performed every year by Nanda and other gopas to please Indra, the Lord of rains and hence conducive to त्रिवर्ग। कृष्ण explained that rain was the work of nature, and that no credit went to Indra. So he persuaded them to worship cows, ब्राह्मणस् and hills. So it hap- pened. Indra who was thus deprived of his बलि grew wrath- ful and sent down a continuous heavy downpour of rain creating panic in the minds of gopas. कृष्ण took hold of the hill Govardhana and held it aloft as an umbrella steadily for seven days. Astonished at this, Indra withdrew his rains and Govardhana was planted in its place. भा. X. २४ (whole); ch. २५. 1-२८.
--the world of Indra. See also ‘Realm of’ under इन्द्र (footnote ४४). M. २७७. २२; २७८. २९; वा. ३४. ७६-7; ६१. ८८; १११. ५२. [page१-197+ २६]
